styles.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
styles.definition: Red wine grape of Bordeaux origin, a natural cross of Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc; thick-skinned and tannic, widely planted worldwide.

styles.name: Merlot
styles.definition: Red wine grape from Bordeaux, softer and earlier-ripening than Cabernet Sauvignon; a major blending partner on Bordeaux's Right Bank.

styles.name: Pinot Noir
styles.definition: Thin-skinned red grape of Burgundy, also a core Champagne grape; known for light-to-medium body and sensitivity to site.

styles.name: Syrah/Shiraz
styles.definition: Red grape from the northern Rhône (Syrah), called Shiraz in Australia; deeply colored with peppery, dark-fruit character.

styles.name: Grenache/Garnacha
styles.definition: Warm-climate red grape (Garnacha in Spain), central to Southern Rhône blends and Priorat.

styles.name: Tempranillo
styles.definition: Spain's leading red grape, the backbone of Rioja and Ribera del Duero (where it is called Tinto Fino).

styles.name: Sangiovese
styles.definition: Italy's most planted red grape and the base of Chianti, Brunello di Montalcino and Vino Nobile.

styles.name: Nebbiolo
styles.definition: Late-ripening, high-tannin, high-acid red grape of Piedmont, used for Barolo and Barbaresco.

styles.name: Malbec
styles.definition: Red grape originally from southwest France (Cahors), now best known from Argentina.

styles.name: Zinfandel/Primitivo
styles.definition: Red grape genetically identical to Croatian Tribidrag; known as Zinfandel in California and Primitivo in Puglia.

styles.name: Cabernet Franc
styles.definition: Red grape from Bordeaux and the Loire; a parent of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot.

styles.name: Gamay
styles.definition: Red grape of Beaujolais, making light, fruity reds.

styles.name: Barbera
styles.definition: High-acid, low-tannin red grape of Piedmont, Italy (e.g. Barbera d'Asti, Barbera d'Alba).

styles.name: Mourvèdre/Monastrell
styles.definition: Late-ripening red grape of Spain (Monastrell) and southern France (Mourvèdre, e.g. Bandol).

styles.name: Chardonnay
styles.definition: White grape of Burgundy and Champagne; flexible in style from lean and unoaked to rich and barrel-fermented.

styles.name: Sauvignon Blanc
styles.definition: Aromatic white grape from the Loire and Bordeaux, typically high in acidity with herbaceous or citrus aromas.

styles.name: Riesling
styles.definition: Aromatic white grape most associated with Germany and Alsace; high acidity, made from bone-dry to very sweet.

styles.name: Pinot Grigio/Gris
styles.definition: Grey-pink-skinned mutation of Pinot Noir; called Pinot Grigio in Italy and Pinot Gris in France.

styles.name: Chenin Blanc
styles.definition: High-acid white grape of the Loire Valley, made dry, sweet and sparkling; also important in South Africa.

styles.name: Gewürztraminer
styles.definition: Very aromatic, pink-skinned white grape (an aromatic form of Savagnin), notable in Alsace.

styles.name: Viognier
styles.definition: Aromatic white grape of the northern Rhône (Condrieu).

styles.name: Albariño
styles.definition: Aromatic, high-acid white grape of Rías Baixas (Spain), called Alvarinho in Portugal.

styles.name: Grüner Veltliner
styles.definition: Austria's signature white grape, often with peppery notes.

styles.name: Sémillon
styles.definition: White grape of Bordeaux, the main grape of Sauternes and prone to noble rot.

styles.name: Torrontés
styles.definition: Aromatic white grape and Argentina's signature white.

styles.name: Assyrtiko
styles.definition: High-acid white grape originally from the Greek island of Santorini, making mineral, dry whites.

styles.name: Provence rosé
styles.definition: Pale dry rosé from Provence, France's largest rosé-producing region.

styles.name: Tavel
styles.definition: Rhône appellation that makes only rosé.

styles.name: Rosado (Navarra)
styles.definition: Spanish rosé tradition of Navarra, typically made from Garnacha.

styles.name: Rosato
styles.definition: Italian term for rosé.

styles.name: White Zinfandel
styles.definition: Off-dry pink wine from Zinfandel, popularized in California in the 1970s–80s.

styles.name: Champagne
styles.definition: Traditional-method sparkling wine from the Champagne AOC in France.

styles.name: Crémant
styles.definition: French traditional-method sparkling wine made outside Champagne (e.g. Alsace, Loire, Burgundy, Jura).

styles.name: Cava
styles.definition: Spanish traditional-method sparkling wine (DO Cava), mostly from Catalonia.

styles.name: Prosecco
styles.definition: Italian sparkling wine from Glera grapes, usually made by the tank method.

styles.name: Franciacorta
styles.definition: Traditional-method sparkling wine DOCG from Lombardy, Italy. It is made mainly from Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

styles.name: Sekt
styles.definition: German and Austrian term for sparkling wine.

styles.name: Pét-nat (ancestral method)
styles.definition: 'Pétillant naturel', a sparkling wine made by the ancestral method.

styles.name: Lambrusco
styles.definition: Family of red grapes and frizzante wines from Emilia-Romagna.

styles.name: Moscato d'Asti
styles.definition: Lightly sparkling, sweet, low-alcohol wine from Moscato Bianco grapes in Piedmont.

styles.name: Georgian qvevri (Rkatsiteli)
styles.definition: Georgian tradition of fermenting and aging wine, often with skins, in large buried clay vessels (qvevri). It is on UNESCO's intangible-heritage list.

styles.name: Friulian Ribolla Gialla
styles.definition: White grape of Friuli and Slovenia (Rebula), often made in skin-contact amber styles.

styles.name: Slovenian (Brda) skin-contact
styles.definition: Amber or orange wines from Goriška Brda, Slovenia, made from white grapes macerated on their skins.

styles.name: Port (Ruby/Tawny/Vintage)
styles.definition: Fortified wine from the Douro Valley, Portugal. Ruby styles keep fresh fruit, Tawny styles are aged oxidatively in wood, and Vintage Port comes from a single de

styles.name: Sherry (Fino/Manzanilla/Amontillado/Oloroso/PX)
styles.definition: Fortified wines from the Jerez area of Andalusia, aged in soleras. Fino and Manzanilla age under flor, Oloroso ages oxidatively, Amontillado does both, and PX i

styles.name: Madeira
styles.definition: Fortified wine from the Portuguese island of Madeira. It is aged with heat and oxygen, making it very long-lived.

styles.name: Marsala
styles.definition: Fortified wine from western Sicily, made dry to sweet in several aging categories.

styles.name: Vermouth
styles.definition: Aromatized wine flavored with botanicals, traditionally including wormwood.

styles.name: Vin doux naturel
styles.definition: French fortified sweet wine made by mutage (adding spirit during fermentation), e.g. Banyuls.

styles.name: Sauternes
styles.definition: Sweet white Bordeaux wine from Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc affected by noble rot.

styles.name: Tokaji Aszú
styles.definition: Hungarian sweet wine made by adding botrytized (aszú) berries to base wine or must.

styles.name: Icewine/Eiswein
styles.definition: Sweet wine made from grapes frozen naturally on the vine and pressed while frozen.

styles.name: Beerenauslese/TBA
styles.definition: German/Austrian Prädikat levels for sweet wines from individually selected overripe berries, often affected by noble rot. Trockenbeerenauslese (TBA) uses shrive

styles.name: Vin Santo
styles.definition: Tuscan dessert wine made from dried grapes and aged in small casks (caratelli).

styles.name: Recioto
styles.definition: Sweet wine of the Veneto made from dried grapes (appassimento), e.g. Recioto della Valpolicella.

styles.name: Late harvest
styles.definition: Grapes picked later than normal for higher sugar, used to make sweeter wines.

styles.name: Tannat
styles.definition: Very tannic red grape of Madiran, France, and Uruguay's signature grape.

styles.name: Petit Verdot
styles.definition: Late-ripening red Bordeaux grape, used in small amounts for color and tannin.

styles.name: Carignan
styles.definition: Late-ripening, high-acid, high-tannin red grape (Cariñena/Mazuelo in Spain). It is common in southern France, Priorat and Sardinia.

styles.name: Cinsault
styles.definition: Heat-tolerant red grape of southern France, used widely in rosé and light reds. It is a parent of Pinotage.

styles.name: Pinot Meunier
styles.definition: Red grape related to Pinot Noir, with downy leaves. It is one of Champagne's three main grapes.

styles.name: Négrette
styles.definition: Red grape of Fronton, southwest France.

styles.name: Mondeuse
styles.definition: Red grape of Savoie, France.

styles.name: Poulsard
styles.definition: Pale-skinned red grape of the Jura (also called Ploussard).

styles.name: Trousseau
styles.definition: Red grape of the Jura, also grown in Portugal as Bastardo.

styles.name: Fer Servadou
styles.definition: Red grape of southwest France (e.g. Marcillac), also called Mansois or Braucol.

styles.name: Aglianico
styles.definition: Tannic southern Italian red grape used for Taurasi and Aglianico del Vulture.

styles.name: Nero d'Avola
styles.definition: Sicily's leading red grape.

styles.name: Montepulciano
styles.definition: Red grape widely planted in central Italy (e.g. Montepulciano d'Abruzzo). It is not related to the Tuscan town of Montepulciano.

styles.name: Dolcetto
styles.definition: Early-ripening red grape of Piedmont, making soft, fruity reds for early drinking.

styles.name: Corvina
styles.definition: Main red grape of Valpolicella, Bardolino and Amarone.

styles.name: Lagrein
styles.definition: Red grape of Alto Adige, Italy.

styles.name: Sagrantino
styles.definition: Very tannic red grape of Montefalco, Umbria.

styles.name: Nerello Mascalese
styles.definition: Red grape of Etna, Sicily, making pale, perfumed reds.

styles.name: Teroldego
styles.definition: Red grape of Trentino, Italy.

styles.name: Schiava
styles.definition: Red grape of Alto Adige (Vernatsch, Trollinger), making light reds.

styles.name: Mencía
styles.definition: Red grape of northwest Spain (Bierzo, Ribeira Sacra), identical to Portugal's Jaen.

styles.name: Bobal
styles.definition: Red grape of Utiel-Requena in Valencia, Spain. It is deeply colored and used for reds and rosés.

styles.name: Graciano
styles.definition: Red grape of Rioja, used in small amounts for acidity, color and aroma.

styles.name: Prieto Picudo
styles.definition: Red grape of León, Spain.

styles.name: Touriga Nacional
styles.definition: Portuguese red grape, a key Port and Douro variety.

styles.name: Touriga Franca
styles.definition: Widely planted Port and Douro red grape.

styles.name: Baga
styles.definition: Thick-skinned, high-acid, tannic red grape of Bairrada, Portugal. It is also used for sparkling wine.

styles.name: Castelão
styles.definition: Widely planted red grape of southern Portugal, also called Periquita.

styles.name: Blaufränkisch
styles.definition: Central European red grape, Austria's leading red in Burgenland and called Kékfrankos in Hungary. It typically makes peppery, dark-fruited, fresh reds.

styles.name: Zweigelt
styles.definition: Austria's most planted red grape, a cross of Blaufränkisch and St. Laurent.

styles.name: St. Laurent
styles.definition: Austrian red grape related to the Pinot family, a parent of Zweigelt.

styles.name: Kadarka
styles.definition: Red grape of Hungary and the Balkans, traditionally used in Bikavér.

styles.name: Plavac Mali
styles.definition: Croatian red grape of the Dalmatian coast, an offspring of Tribidrag (Zinfandel).

styles.name: Xinomavro
styles.definition: High-acid, tannic red grape of Naoussa, northern Greece.

styles.name: Agiorgitiko
styles.definition: Red grape of Nemea in the Peloponnese, Greece. It makes soft, fruity reds as well as rosés.

styles.name: Fetească Neagră
styles.definition: Indigenous red grape of Romania and Moldova.

styles.name: Mavrud
styles.definition: Indigenous red grape of Bulgaria (Thracian Valley).

styles.name: Carménère (Chile)
styles.definition: Red Bordeaux grape that is now rare in France. It survived in Chile, where it was long mistaken for Merlot until identified in 1994.

styles.name: País (Chile)
styles.definition: Historic red grape of Chile, brought by Spanish settlers (Listán Prieto in Spain).

styles.name: Pinotage (South Africa)
styles.definition: South African red cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault (then called Hermitage), created in 1925.

styles.name: Bonarda (Argentina)
styles.definition: Argentina's widely planted red Bonarda, identified as Douce Noir (Corbeau) from Savoie. It is not the same as Italian Bonarda.

styles.name: Marsanne
styles.definition: White grape of the northern Rhône (Hermitage, Saint-Joseph), often blended with Roussanne.

styles.name: Roussanne
styles.definition: Aromatic white grape of the northern Rhône, often blended with Marsanne.

styles.name: Melon de Bourgogne
styles.definition: White grape of Muscadet in the western Loire, often aged on its lees (sur lie).

styles.name: Aligoté
styles.definition: White grape of Burgundy, typically high in acidity. It is used for Bourgogne Aligoté and, traditionally, for the Kir cocktail.

styles.name: Petit Manseng
styles.definition: White grape of Jurançon with small, thick-skinned berries, used for sweet and dry wines.

styles.name: Gros Manseng
styles.definition: White grape of southwest France (Jurançon, Gascony), used for dry and sweet wines.

styles.name: Savagnin
styles.definition: Jura white grape used for Vin Jaune. It is the same variety as Traminer.

styles.name: Picpoul
styles.definition: Grape of the Languedoc, best known for high-acid Picpoul de Pinet whites.

styles.name: Clairette
styles.definition: White grape of southern France, used for Clairette de Die sparkling wine and in Rhône blends.

styles.name: Mauzac
styles.definition: White grape of Gaillac and Limoux, used in Blanquette de Limoux.

styles.name: Garganega
styles.definition: Main white grape of Soave, Veneto.

styles.name: Vermentino
styles.definition: White grape of Sardinia, Liguria and Provence (Rolle).

styles.name: Fiano
styles.definition: White grape of Campania, Italy, best known for Fiano di Avellino.

styles.name: Greco
styles.definition: White grape of Campania, Italy (e.g. Greco di Tufo).

styles.name: Falanghina
styles.definition: Ancient white grape of Campania, Italy.

styles.name: Cortese
styles.definition: White grape of Piedmont, used for Gavi.

styles.name: Arneis
styles.definition: White grape of Roero in Piedmont, Italy, making aromatic, medium-bodied dry whites.

styles.name: Trebbiano
styles.definition: Family of high-yield white Italian grapes (Ugni Blanc in France).

styles.name: Verdicchio
styles.definition: White grape of the Marche, Italy.

styles.name: Friulano
styles.definition: White grape of Friuli, Italy, formerly called Tocai Friulano (identical to Sauvignonasse).

styles.name: Verdejo
styles.definition: White grape of Rueda, Spain.

styles.name: Godello
styles.definition: White grape of northwest Spain (Valdeorras, Bierzo).

styles.name: Macabeo (Viura)
styles.definition: White grape of Spain (called Viura in Rioja), one of the classic Cava grapes.

styles.name: Xarel·lo
styles.definition: Catalan white grape, one of the three traditional Cava grapes.

styles.name: Parellada
styles.definition: White Catalan grape, one of the three traditional Cava grapes.

styles.name: Palomino
styles.definition: White grape that makes most Sherry.

styles.name: Loureiro
styles.definition: Aromatic white grape of Vinho Verde, Portugal.

styles.name: Arinto
styles.definition: Portuguese white grape that keeps high acidity even in warm climates. It is important in Bucelas and Vinho Verde (as Pedernã).

styles.name: Encruzado
styles.definition: White grape of the Dão region, Portugal, used for structured dry whites.

styles.name: Furmint
styles.definition: High-acid white grape that is the main variety of Tokaji.

styles.name: Hárslevelű
styles.definition: Hungarian white grape, the second main grape of Tokaji.

styles.name: Welschriesling
styles.definition: Central European white grape (Graševina, Olaszrizling), unrelated to Riesling.

styles.name: Silvaner
styles.definition: White grape grown mainly in Franken and Rheinhessen, Germany, and in Alsace (Sylvaner).

styles.name: Müller-Thurgau
styles.definition: White cross of Riesling and Madeleine Royale, bred in Geisenheim in 1882. It is high-yielding and early-ripening.

styles.name: Kerner
styles.definition: German white cross of Trollinger (Schiava) and Riesling.

styles.name: Rkatsiteli
styles.definition: High-acid white grape of Georgia, widely planted across the former USSR.

styles.name: Moschofilero
styles.definition: Pink-skinned aromatic Greek grape of Mantinia, Peloponnese.

styles.name: Malagousia
styles.definition: Aromatic Greek white grape revived from near-extinction in the late 20th century.

styles.name: Muscat of Alexandria
styles.definition: Ancient aromatic white Muscat grape, used for wine, table grapes and raisins.

styles.name: Colombard
styles.definition: White grape of southwest France, used for Cognac and Armagnac distillation and for fresh whites such as Côtes de Gascogne.

styles.name: Chasselas
styles.definition: White grape most associated with Switzerland (Fendant in Valais). It makes delicate, low-acid dry whites.

styles.name: Petite Arvine
styles.definition: White grape of the Valais, Switzerland.

styles.name: Concord
styles.definition: Vitis labrusca-derived American grape with 'foxy' flavor, widely used for juice.

styles.name: Catawba
styles.definition: American pink-red grape of Vitis labrusca heritage. It was historically important for 19th-century Ohio sparkling wine.

styles.name: Niagara
styles.definition: White American grape of labrusca type, used for sweet wine and juice.

styles.name: Isabella
styles.definition: American hybrid grape of Vitis labrusca origin, with 'foxy' flavor.

styles.name: Ives
styles.definition: American red grape of labrusca type, historically used in the eastern US.

styles.name: Vitis riparia (riverbank grape)
styles.definition: North American vine species, cold-hardy and phylloxera-resistant, used as a rootstock parent.

styles.name: Vitis rupestris (rock grape)
styles.definition: North American vine species, deep-rooting, used as a rootstock parent.

styles.name: Vitis berlandieri
styles.definition: North American vine species native to Texas, valued as a rootstock parent for lime tolerance.

styles.name: Mainly rootstock parents — see Rootstocks
styles.definition: These American Vitis species are used mainly as parents of phylloxera-resistant rootstocks, not for wine; see the Rootstocks group.

styles.name: Scuppernong
styles.definition: Bronze muscadine (Vitis rotundifolia) variety, the original muscadine named in North Carolina.

styles.name: Carlos
styles.definition: Bronze-skinned muscadine (Vitis rotundifolia) variety grown in the southeastern US for wine and juice.

styles.name: Noble
styles.definition: Spanish legal aging term (Ley 24/2003) for wine aged at least 18 months in total.

styles.name: Magnolia
styles.definition: Bronze-skinned muscadine variety grown in the southeastern US.

styles.name: Norton (Cynthiana)
styles.definition: Native American red grape (Vitis aestivalis lineage), Missouri's state grape.

styles.name: Seyval Blanc
styles.definition: French-American hybrid white grape grown in England, New York and Canada.

styles.name: Vidal Blanc
styles.definition: French-American hybrid white grape, widely used for Canadian icewine.

styles.name: Chambourcin
styles.definition: French-American hybrid red grape, popular in the eastern US for its disease resistance and deep color.

styles.name: Baco Noir
styles.definition: French-American hybrid red grape bred by François Baco from Folle Blanche and a Vitis riparia. It is grown in cool climates such as Ontario and New York.

styles.name: Maréchal Foch
styles.definition: French-American hybrid red grape suited to cool climates.

styles.name: Traminette
styles.definition: Hybrid white grape from Gewürztraminer parentage, bred in the US.

styles.name: Marquette
styles.definition: Cold-hardy red hybrid grape from the University of Minnesota, a grandchild of Pinot Noir.

styles.name: Frontenac
styles.definition: Cold-hardy red hybrid grape from the University of Minnesota.

styles.name: La Crescent
styles.definition: Cold-hardy white hybrid grape from the University of Minnesota, with apricot-citrus aromas.

styles.name: Regent
styles.definition: German fungus-resistant (PIWI) red grape bred at Geilweilerhof.

styles.name: Solaris
styles.definition: Early-ripening German fungus-resistant (PIWI) white grape, suited to very cool climates.

styles.name: Johanniter
styles.definition: German fungus-resistant (PIWI) white grape bred at Freiburg with Riesling as a parent.

styles.name: Souvignier Gris
styles.definition: German fungus-resistant (PIWI) white grape bred at Freiburg.

styles.name: Cabernet Cortis
styles.definition: German fungus-resistant (PIWI) red grape bred at Freiburg with Cabernet Sauvignon as a parent.

styles.name: Muscaris
styles.definition: German fungus-resistant (PIWI) aromatic white grape with Solaris and Muscat parentage.

styles.name: Divico
styles.definition: Swiss fungus-resistant red grape bred by Agroscope, with Gamaret as a parent.

styles.name: Pinot Noir Dijon 115
styles.definition: Widely planted Burgundian 'Dijon' clone of Pinot Noir.

styles.name: Pinot Noir Dijon 667
styles.definition: Burgundian 'Dijon' clone of Pinot Noir with small clusters.

styles.name: Pinot Noir Dijon 777
styles.definition: Burgundian 'Dijon' clone of Pinot Noir, known for deep color and dark fruit.

styles.name: Pinot Noir Pommard (UCD 4)
styles.definition: Pinot Noir selection from Burgundy distributed by UC Davis, important in Oregon and California.

styles.name: Pinot Noir Wädenswil (UCD 1A)
styles.definition: Swiss-origin Pinot Noir selection distributed by UC Davis.

styles.name: Chardonnay Dijon 76
styles.definition: One of the Burgundian 'Dijon' clones of Chardonnay, selected in France and widely planted in Oregon and elsewhere.

styles.name: Chardonnay Dijon 96
styles.definition: A Burgundian 'Dijon' clone of Chardonnay, used for still and sparkling wine.

styles.name: Chardonnay Wente
styles.definition: The Wente selection, the historic Chardonnay clonal lineage behind much of California's Chardonnay. It is known for small, uneven ('hen and chicken') berries.

styles.name: Cabernet Sauvignon 337
styles.definition: A widely planted French certified clone of Cabernet Sauvignon. It is known for small clusters and concentrated fruit.

styles.name: Sangiovese Grosso (Brunello)
styles.definition: Local name for the Sangiovese biotype used for Brunello di Montalcino.

styles.name: Pinot Gris (from Pinot Noir)
styles.definition: Pink-grey-skinned color mutation of Pinot Noir.

styles.name: Pinot Blanc
styles.definition: White mutation of Pinot Noir, grown in Alsace, Italy (Pinot Bianco) and Germany (Weissburgunder).

styles.name: Pinot Meunier (chimera)
styles.definition: Meunier is a periclinal chimera: its outer cell layer carries a mutation that the inner tissue of Pinot Noir lacks.

styles.name: Grenache Blanc
styles.definition: White-skinned form of Grenache, used in the Rhône, Roussillon and Spain.

styles.name: Grenache Gris
styles.definition: Grey-pink-skinned form of Grenache, notable in Roussillon.

styles.name: Gewürztraminer (aromatic Savagnin Rose)
styles.definition: Very aromatic, pink-skinned white grape (an aromatic form of Savagnin), notable in Alsace.

styles.name: Chardonnay Musqué
styles.definition: Aromatic, Muscat-scented clonal variants of Chardonnay.

styles.name: Sauvignon Gris
styles.definition: Pink-skinned mutation of Sauvignon Blanc.

styles.name: Alicante Bouschet
styles.definition: Teinturier (red-fleshed) grape bred from Petit Bouschet and Grenache.

styles.name: Saperavi
styles.definition: Teinturier red grape of Georgia, deeply colored.

styles.name: Petit Bouschet
styles.definition: Teinturier red grape bred by Louis Bouschet from Aramon and Teinturier du Cher. It is a parent of Alicante Bouschet.

styles.name: Grand Noir de la Calmette
styles.definition: Teinturier red grape bred by Henri Bouschet.

styles.name: Gamay de Bouze
styles.definition: Teinturier (red-fleshed) mutation of Gamay.

styles.name: Rubired
styles.definition: Californian teinturier hybrid grape, used for color and juice.

styles.name: Riparia Gloire de Montpellier
styles.definition: Pure Vitis riparia rootstock selection. Low vigor and early ripening, suited to fertile soils.

styles.name: Rupestris du Lot (St. George)
styles.definition: Vitis rupestris rootstock, deep-rooting and vigorous.

styles.name: 3309 Couderc
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis riparia × V. rupestris cross. Moderately low in vigor and widely used in cool, deep, well-watered soils; it handles drought and lime poor

styles.name: 101-14 Millardet et de Grasset
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis riparia × V. rupestris cross, bred in France in the 1880s. It is low-vigor and advances ripening, suited to fertile, moist soils, but it

styles.name: Schwarzmann
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis riparia × V. rupestris cross with some nematode tolerance.

styles.name: 5BB Kober
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. riparia cross, selected by Kober in Austria. It is vigorous and lime-tolerant.

styles.name: SO4
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. riparia cross (Selection Oppenheim 4).

styles.name: 5C Teleki
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. riparia cross, selected in Hungary. Moderate vigor and early ripening.

styles.name: 420A Millardet et de Grasset
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. riparia cross. Low vigor, lime-tolerant and slow to establish; common in Champagne and Burgundy.

styles.name: 110 Richter
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. rupestris cross. It is vigorous and drought-tolerant, widely used in dry Mediterranean vineyards.

styles.name: 1103 Paulsen
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. rupestris cross, bred in Sicily. It is vigorous and tolerates drought and moderate salinity.

styles.name: 140 Ruggeri
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. rupestris cross, bred in Sicily. It is very vigorous and tolerates drought and limestone soils.

styles.name: 99 Richter
styles.definition: Rootstock from a Vitis berlandieri × V. rupestris cross. Vigorous and drought-tolerant, used in warm regions.

styles.name: Freedom
styles.definition: Nematode-resistant rootstock with Vitis champinii in its parentage, used in California.

styles.name: Harmony
styles.definition: Nematode-resistant rootstock used in California.

styles.name: Dog Ridge
styles.definition: Vigorous rootstock selection of Vitis champinii, tolerant of nematodes and drought.

styles.name: Ramsey (Salt Creek)
styles.definition: Very vigorous Vitis champinii rootstock, tolerant of nematodes, drought and salinity.

styles.name: 1616 Couderc
styles.definition: Rootstock bred in France from a Vitis solonis × V. riparia cross. It is low-vigor and tolerates wet and somewhat saline soils.

styles.name: Own-rooted (ungrafted)
styles.definition: A vine growing on its own roots rather than grafted onto a rootstock.

styles.name: Single Guyot
styles.definition: Cane-pruning system that keeps one cane plus a renewal spur.

styles.name: Double Guyot
styles.definition: Cane-pruning system that keeps two canes, one trained each way along the wire.

styles.name: Bilateral cordon (spur-pruned)
styles.definition: Vine training in which a permanent arm (cordon) extends in two directions along a wire. Short spurs on the cordon are pruned each winter.

styles.name: Vertical shoot positioning (VSP)
styles.definition: Trellis system where shoots are trained upward in a narrow vertical curtain.

styles.name: Gobelet (bush vine)
styles.definition: Free-standing vine trained without wires into a goblet shape, common in hot, dry regions.

styles.name: Pergola
styles.definition: Overhead trellis system, traditional in parts of Italy and northwest Spain.

styles.name: Lyre
styles.definition: Divided-canopy trellis shaped like a U or lyre.

styles.name: Scott Henry
styles.definition: Divided vertical trellis with upper shoots trained up and lower shoots trained down.

styles.name: Smart-Dyson
styles.definition: Divided vertical trellis with upward and downward shoots, devised by Richard Smart and John Dyson.

styles.name: Geneva Double Curtain
styles.definition: Divided-canopy trellis developed at Geneva, New York, with two hanging curtains of shoots.

styles.name: Sprawl
styles.definition: Training with little shoot positioning, letting the canopy hang freely.

styles.name: Cane pruning
styles.definition: Winter pruning that keeps one or two of last year's canes and ties them along the wire to bear the new crop. The Guyot system is an example.

styles.name: Spur pruning
styles.definition: Winter pruning of last year's canes down to short spurs on a permanent cordon.

styles.name: Shoot thinning
styles.definition: Removing excess or poorly placed shoots early in the season.

styles.name: Shoot positioning
styles.definition: Training the season's new shoots into place on the trellis.

styles.name: Leaf removal
styles.definition: Removing leaves around the grape clusters to improve air flow and sun exposure.

styles.name: Hedging (topping)
styles.definition: Trimming the tops and sides of the vine canopy during the growing season.

styles.name: Green harvest (crop thinning)
styles.definition: Removing some unripe bunches to reduce yield and concentrate the rest.

styles.name: Cover crops
styles.definition: Plants grown between vine rows to manage soil erosion, structure, water and vine vigor.

styles.name: Destemming
styles.definition: Separating grape berries from their stems before crushing or fermentation.

styles.name: Whole-cluster fermentation
styles.definition: Fermenting red grapes with their stems still attached.

styles.name: Cold soak
styles.definition: Holding crushed red grapes cold before fermentation to extract color and aroma.

styles.name: Carbonic maceration
styles.definition: Whole, uncrushed grapes ferment inside a CO2-filled vessel, giving fruity, low-tannin reds (as in Beaujolais).

styles.name: Pump-over (remontage)
styles.definition: Pumping fermenting red wine from the bottom of the tank over the skin cap to extract color and tannin.

styles.name: Punch-down (pigeage)
styles.definition: Pushing the floating skin cap down into fermenting red wine to extract color and tannin.

styles.name: Délestage (rack & return)
styles.definition: Draining fermenting red juice off the skins into another tank, then pouring it back over the cap to extract gently.

styles.name: Extended maceration
styles.definition: Leaving red wine on its skins after fermentation ends to change tannin texture.

styles.name: Saignée
styles.definition: Bleeding off juice from a red-wine tank early to make rosé and concentrate the remaining red.

styles.name: Malolactic conversion
styles.definition: Bacterial conversion of malic acid into lactic acid, softening a wine's acidity.

styles.name: Whole-bunch pressing
styles.definition: Pressing whole clusters without crushing, giving cleaner, lower-phenolic juice.

styles.name: Skin contact
styles.definition: Leaving juice in contact with grape skins; for white grapes this makes 'orange' or amber wine.

styles.name: Cold settling (débourbage)
styles.definition: Letting freshly pressed white juice rest cold so solids settle out before fermentation.

styles.name: Cool fermentation
styles.definition: Fermenting at low temperatures (often around 10–16 °C for whites) to keep fresh, fruity aromas.

styles.name: Lees aging (sur lie)
styles.definition: Leaving wine in contact with its spent yeast after fermentation to build texture and flavor.

styles.name: Bâtonnage
styles.definition: Stirring the lees (spent yeast) back into a wine during aging to add texture.

styles.name: Direct-press rosé
styles.definition: Rosé made by pressing red grapes right away, giving brief skin contact and pale color.

styles.name: Blocked malolactic
styles.definition: Preventing malolactic fermentation (for example by cold, sulfur dioxide or filtration) so the wine keeps its sharper malic acidity.

styles.name: Traditional method
styles.definition: Sparkling method in which the second fermentation happens in the bottle sold (as in Champagne and Cava).

styles.name: Tank (Charmat) method
styles.definition: Sparkling method with the second fermentation in a pressurized tank (common for Prosecco).

styles.name: Ancestral method
styles.definition: Sparkling method where wine is bottled before primary fermentation finishes, trapping its CO2.

styles.name: Transfer method
styles.definition: Sparkling method with second fermentation in bottle, after which the wine is transferred to a tank, filtered and rebottled.

styles.name: Riddling (remuage)
styles.definition: Gradually turning and tilting sparkling-wine bottles so sediment collects in the neck before disgorgement.

styles.name: Disgorgement
styles.definition: Removing the frozen plug of yeast sediment from a traditional-method sparkling wine bottle.

styles.name: Dosage
styles.definition: Sugar-and-wine mixture added after disgorgement, setting a sparkling wine's sweetness level.

styles.name: Carbonation
styles.definition: Presence of dissolved CO2, which makes wine sparkling. It comes either from a second fermentation or from injected gas.

styles.name: Mutage (fortification during fermentation)
styles.definition: Stopping fermentation by adding grape spirit, leaving natural sugar (used for Port and vins doux naturels).

styles.name: Post-fermentation fortification
styles.definition: Adding spirit after fermentation has finished, leaving a dry base that may be sweetened later. Sherry is the classic example.

styles.name: Flor (biological aging)
styles.definition: A layer of yeast on the surface of Fino and Manzanilla Sherry that protects the wine from oxidation.

styles.name: Oxidative aging
styles.definition: Aging with deliberate oxygen contact, giving nutty, dried-fruit flavors (e.g. Oloroso, tawny Port).

styles.name: Estufagem (Madeira)
styles.definition: Madeira method of heating wine in tanks (estufas) to speed up aging.

styles.name: Fining
styles.definition: Adding an agent (such as bentonite or egg white) that binds and removes haze or harsh compounds.

styles.name: Filtration
styles.definition: Passing wine through a filter medium to remove yeast, bacteria or haze before bottling.

styles.name: Cold stabilization
styles.definition: Chilling wine so tartrate crystals form and can be removed before bottling.

styles.name: Blending
styles.definition: Combining wines from different grapes, vineyards, vessels or vintages to build balance and a consistent style.

styles.name: American white oak (Quercus alba)
styles.definition: The main American barrel oak. Its staves are usually sawn rather than split, and it typically gives stronger vanilla and coconut notes than French oak.

styles.name: French sessile oak (Q. petraea)
styles.definition: European oak species with tighter grain and more aromatic compounds, widely preferred for wine barrels.

styles.name: French pedunculate oak (Q. robur)
styles.definition: European oak species, more porous and higher in tannin than sessile oak. It is traditionally preferred for spirits such as Cognac.

styles.name: Hungarian oak (Q. petraea)
styles.definition: Sessile oak from Hungary's forests (e.g. Zemplén), used for barrels.

styles.name: Oregon oak (Q. garryana)
styles.definition: Oak native to the Pacific Northwest, sometimes used for wine barrels.

styles.name: Mizunara (Q. mongolica, Japan)
styles.definition: Japanese oak used for whisky casks. It is porous and hard to work, and is associated with sandalwood and incense aromas.

styles.name: Acacia (black locust)
styles.definition: Wood of the black locust tree (Robinia pseudoacacia), sometimes used for white-wine barrels. It is commonly described as giving floral notes with little oak-sty

styles.name: Chestnut (Castanea sativa)
styles.definition: Sweet chestnut wood, historically used for barrels in Italy and France. It is porous and low in aromatic compounds, so it allows oxygen exchange.

styles.name: Cherry (Prunus avium)
styles.definition: Cherry wood, occasionally used for casks. It is commonly described as oxidizing wine faster and adding fruity, lightly sweet notes.

styles.name: Amburana (Brazil)
styles.definition: Brazilian hardwood (Amburana cearensis) used for casks, especially for cachaça. It gives strong sweet-spice aromas often compared to cinnamon.

styles.name: Allier
styles.definition: French département whose forests (including Tronçais) supply tight-grained sessile oak prized for wine barrels.

styles.name: Tronçais (Allier)
styles.definition: Famous oak forest in the Allier, France, planted under Colbert, with tight-grained oak.

styles.name: Nevers
styles.definition: Oak forests of the Nièvre, France, known for fine-grained oak.

styles.name: Bertranges
styles.definition: Oak forest in the Nièvre, France, known for fine-grained sessile oak for barrels.

styles.name: Vosges
styles.definition: Oak forests of the Vosges mountains, France, used for barrels.

styles.name: Limousin (wide grain, Cognac)
styles.definition: Oak forests near Limoges, France, with wide-grained, tannic oak traditionally used for Cognac.

styles.name: Jupilles
styles.definition: Oak forest in the Sarthe, France, used for barrels.

styles.name: Open-air seasoning (typically 24–36 months)
styles.definition: Drying barrel staves outdoors so rain and sun leach harsh tannins before coopering.

styles.name: Kiln-dried staves
styles.definition: Barrel staves dried quickly in kilns rather than seasoned outdoors.

styles.name: Rain & sun leaching of harsh tannins
styles.definition: The effect of outdoor seasoning on staves: weather washes out bitter tannins and starts breaking down wood compounds.

styles.name: Light toast
styles.definition: Barrel interior toasted briefly, keeping fresh wood character and less roasted flavor.

styles.name: Medium toast
styles.definition: Middle toast level for barrels, balancing fresh oak with vanilla and toasty notes.

styles.name: Medium-plus toast
styles.definition: Toast level between medium and heavy, giving more caramel and spice.

styles.name: Heavy toast
styles.definition: Barrel interior toasted long and hot, giving roasted, smoky, coffee-like flavors.

styles.name: Toasted heads
styles.definition: Barrel ends (heads) toasted like the staves, adding more toast flavor.

styles.name: Untoasted heads
styles.definition: Barrel heads left untoasted, keeping more raw-wood character.

styles.name: See Spirits Academy: char levels
styles.definition: Cross-reference: barrel char levels (#1–#4) are covered in the Spirits Academy.

styles.name: Blood tub (~40 L)
styles.definition: Very small cask of about 40 litres. Its high wood-to-liquid ratio speeds wood extraction.

styles.name: Quarter cask (~125 L)
styles.definition: Small cask that speeds up spirit maturation.

styles.name: American standard barrel (200 L / 53 gal)
styles.definition: The common 53-gallon (~200 L) American oak barrel.

styles.name: Bordeaux barrique (225 L)
styles.definition: Standard 225 L Bordeaux barrel.

styles.name: Burgundy pièce (228 L)
styles.definition: Standard 228 L Burgundy barrel.

styles.name: Hogshead (~250 L)
styles.definition: Cask of around 250 L, often rebuilt from bourbon barrels.

styles.name: Puncheon (~450–500 L)
styles.definition: Large cask used for wine, rum and whisky.

styles.name: Sherry butt (~500 L)
styles.definition: Traditional Sherry cask of around 500 L, often reused to age whisky.

styles.name: Port pipe (~550–650 L)
styles.definition: Traditional Douro cask, used for Port and later often for whisky finishing.

styles.name: Foudre / foeder (1,000 L+)
styles.definition: Large wooden vat, often over 1,000 L. Its low wood-to-liquid ratio gives little oak flavor.

styles.name: New oak
styles.definition: A barrel used for the first time, giving the most oak flavor and tannin.

styles.name: First fill
styles.definition: A cask used for the first time after its previous contents (e.g. first-fill ex-bourbon), giving more flavor than refill casks.

styles.name: Refill (second fill+)
styles.definition: A cask reused after its first fill, giving less flavor each time.

styles.name: Neutral oak (3+ uses)
styles.definition: Barrels used several times that now give little oak flavor but still allow slow oxygen exchange.

styles.name: Rejuvenated (re-toasted/re-charred)
styles.definition: A used cask that has been scraped and re-toasted or re-charred to restore some of its flavor.

styles.name: Percentage new oak (wine élevage)
styles.definition: Share of a wine aged in brand-new barrels, which controls how much oak flavor it gets.

styles.name: Sangria
styles.definition: Spanish punch of wine, fruit, sweetener and often brandy.

styles.name: Spritzer
styles.definition: Wine mixed with sparkling water.

styles.name: Wine cooler
styles.definition: Wine-based drink mixed with fruit juice, sugar and carbonation.

styles.name: Mulled wine
styles.definition: Wine heated with spices, sugar and often citrus.

styles.name: Kalimotxo (wine + cola)
styles.definition: Basque drink of red wine mixed with cola, roughly half and half.

styles.name: Dealcoholized red
styles.definition: Red wine made normally, then with most alcohol removed (e.g. by vacuum distillation or membranes). It is labeled non-alcoholic at or below 0.5% ABV.

styles.name: Dealcoholized white
styles.definition: White wine with most alcohol removed after fermentation, typically to 0.5% ABV or less.

styles.name: Dealcoholized sparkling
styles.definition: Sparkling wine with alcohol removed and carbonation restored, typically to 0.5% ABV or less.

styles.name: Dealcoholized rosé
styles.definition: Rosé wine with most alcohol removed after fermentation, typically to 0.5% ABV or less.
